subject.title: [Bug]: ACP concurrent session spawns — first agent fails to launch CC process

question: Should ACP keep distinct child sessions parallel and fix only the ACPX/Claude launch-readiness race, or should rapid distinct ACPX launches be gated/serialized despite the current concurrency contract?
rationale: Current docs and tests support concurrent distinct ACP sessions, but the reported failure mode may require an owner decision about whether preserving that parallelism is worth the launch-readiness complexity.

options.title: Preserve parallel sessions
options.body: Keep the current distinct-session concurrency contract and require live ACPX/Claude proof before making a targeted launch-readiness fix.

options.title: Gate ACPX launches
options.body: Serialize or throttle rapid ACPX launches when maintainers decide reliability is more important than concurrent child start latency.

options.title: Defer without fix
options.body: Leave the issue parked until a current live reproduction shows the first-child no-output failure on supported versions.

recommendation.title: Preserve parallel sessions
recommendation.body: Keep the current distinct-session concurrency contract and require live ACPX/Claude proof before making a targeted launch-readiness fix.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant ACP spawn/control-plane and acpx integration behavior appears to originate in this contributor's merged ACP feature history.
